premise.title: Why Nepal?
premise.body1:
Nepal is better known for its mountains than its coffee. But among the hills below the Himalaya, coffee has been flourishing for decades.

Grown at elevations between roughly 800 and 1,600 metres, Nepalese coffee benefits from cool temperatures, distinct seasons and abundant monsoon rainfall. 

These conditions allow the cherries to develop slowly, building the foundations for complex and expressive coffees.
premise.body2: This is coffee shaped by Nepal’s landscape: carefully cultivated and unmistakably of its place.

coffee.title: What we ofer
coffee.body1:
We source the very best of Nepali coffee, working with reputable and proven producers. Before delivery to your doorstep, we certify its origins and ensure each lot goes through rigorous quality assurance procedures.

We ensure the farmers who work hard to produce this remarkable product get a fair paycheck. 1% of our profit goes directly back to the farmers.

We source Arabica beans, predominantly Bourbon and Typica. These traditional varieties, combined with Nepal’s distinctive geography and climate, provide the foundation for coffees with clarity, sweetness and lively acidity. 

Nepali coffee represents huge untapped potential, with demand growing rapidly each year. The region is increasingly known for producing coffee of exceptional and outstanding quality. Assessed lots repeatedly scoring above 85 on the 50-100 SCA scale.

In 2020, Nepali Coffee scored 92 in a blind assessment review by Press House Coffee (Californian Trade Magazine), highlighting it as "delicate, balanced and sweet-toned".

about.title: About us
about.aboutBody1: When I first visited Nepal in the summer of 2025, I discovered a side of the country I had not expected: a vibrant and rapidly developing coffee culture.I brought several kilos of roasted Nepali coffee back to the UK to share with friends and family. Their reaction was much the same as mine. The coffee spoke for itself.From coffee shops in Kathmandu and Biratnagar to producers in rural areas, I had the opportunity to taste coffee grown and produced in Nepal. What stood out immediately was the quality in the cup: smooth, rich and often remarkably fruity, with a character that was distinctly its own.As someone who has been passionate about coffee for many years and enjoys exploring coffees from different parts of the world, I found it surprising that Nepal is still relatively unfamiliar to many specialty coffee drinkers. Here was coffee I genuinely enjoyed, from a country with a remarkable growing environment and a coffee industry that is continuing to develop.That first experience led to an idea: to help introduce more people to Nepali coffee and create stronger connections between the producers growing it in Nepal and coffee drinkers around the world.Mewa Valley Coffee was created with that goal in mind. We want to showcase the quality and character of Nepali coffee, while helping bring it to a wider audience beyond Nepal.
about.sourcingBody1: We are in active conversation with several producers at different stages of readiness, from established exporters to farms shipping their first commercial lots. They span the hill districts of Koshi and Lumbini: Gulmi, Bhojpur, Ilam and Solukhumbu.
about.hillAlt: Hills near Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.mapAlt: Map of Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.sourcingBody2: Between them our producers work across washed, natural and yellow honey processing. Predominantly Arabica, with some Robusta at lower altitude in parts of Koshi Province.
about.sourcingBody3: Growing altitudes run from roughly 800 to 1,600 metres. Higher up, the cherry ripens slowly — sugars concentrate and the bean comes out denser.
about.sourcingBody4: We are looking to work with roasters who find that as interesting as we do.
